heroHeadline: Hungary Seals €16.4B EU Deal; Magyar Moves to Constitutionally Remove Sulyok
heroSubtitle: On May 29, PM Péter Magyar and European Commission President von der Leyen signed a €16.4 billion EU funds agreement — €10B RRF and €6.4B cohesion — the largest EU-Hungary unlock in history, capping five weeks of Brussels negotiations. On May 31, both President Tamás Sulyok and Prosecutor General Gábor Bálint Nagy refused Magyar's resignation deadlines, forcing a constitutional showdown. On June 1, Magyar announced a constitutional amendment to create a framework enabling parliamentary removal of fixed-term officeholders, leveraging Tisza's 141-seat supermajority. The amendment — the second use of Tisza's constitutional majority since taking power May 9 — is expected to pass within one month.
